nodes.label: Supporting eco-friendly businesses

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Supporting eco-friendly businesses_qna_000
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What do the initiatives mentioned in the paragraph encourage for businesses?
nodes.answer: The initiatives encourage further business actions towards the development of nature-positive business models.
nodes.paragraph: The initiatives have encouraged further business actions towards the development of nature-positive business models. Such transitions involve complex processes, and they require radical changes in both social and technological systems [7 , 11]. For Dutch farmers, the transition will require moving towards more sustainable production methods in response to challenges (e.g. biodiversity loss and climate change), whilst also maintaining a viable business model. As demonstrated by the Netherlands national taskforce on earning capacity for cir - cular agriculture, the development of new revenue/business models poses a number of major challenges. Stressing the urgent need for a suitable revenue model, this taskforce argues that such models are crucial to the success of the transition towards more sus- tainable agriculture [12]. Within the European context, the same argument has been applied to the development of business models for a circular and sustainable bioecon- omy [13 15]. To help identify critical success factors for the successful implementation of cir - cular and nature-inclusive or nature-positive agricultural business models (CNABM), we build on a framework developed by Antikainen and Valkokari [16] and adapted it according to a synthesis of literature.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Supporting eco-friendly businesses_qna_001
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What are the primary barriers within the internal environment of businesses that limit positive employee behaviour in the context of sustainable production and consumption?
nodes.answer: Organizational barriers such as aversion to change or a lack of priority from top management can limit the development of positive employee behaviour towards sustainable production and consumption initiatives.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Supporting eco-friendly businesses_qna_002
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What did Fauci et al. (2022) discover about the importance of personal norms in the intention of Malaysian tourists to choose green hotels?
nodes.answer: Fauci et al. (2022) found that personal norms are important in generating tourists' intention to choose green hotels, indicating a direct link between personal norms and green behavioural intention.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Supporting eco-friendly businesses_qna_003
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How do close relationships with family, friends, or colleagues who value environmental protection affect individuals' engagement in environmentally friendly behaviour?
nodes.answer: Individuals with close relationships with those who value environmental protection may feel increased pressure to engage in environmentally friendly behaviour, including participating in second-hand fashion behaviours. This social influence from close relationships can shape individuals' intentions and behaviours towards environmental sustainability.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Supporting eco-friendly businesses_qna_004
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What potential impact can encourage environmentally friendly behaviour have on society?
nodes.answer: Encouraging society to value environmentally friendly behaviour can improve environmental ethics, promote sustainable development policies, and positively impact both society and the environment.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Supporting eco-friendly businesses_qna_005
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does the value-belief-emotion-norm model investigate customers' eco-friendly behaviour according to Han, Hwang, & Lee (2016)?
nodes.answer: The value-belief-emotion-norm model, as investigated by Han, Hwang, & Lee (2016), examines how customers' eco-friendly behaviour is influenced by their personal values, beliefs, emotions, and social norms related to sustainability in the context of travel and tourism marketing.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Supporting eco-friendly businesses_qna_006
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What are some psychological factors that can foster pro-environmental behaviours in healthcare organizations?
nodes.answer: Psychological factors such as awareness of environmental issues, personal values related to sustainability, and intrinsic motivation towards eco-friendly practices can foster pro-environmental behaviours in healthcare organizations.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Supporting eco-friendly businesses_qna_007
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How do companies risk falling behind if they do not prioritize sustainable business models?
nodes.answer: Companies risk falling behind if they fail to emphasize sustainable business models because they may overlook integrating sustainable values into their core activities, ultimately impacting competitiveness and responsiveness to changing consumer preferences and regulatory requirements.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Supporting eco-friendly businesses_qna_008
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Why is it important for environmentally friendly businesses to focus on improving green consumption activities?
nodes.answer: Focusing on improving green consumption activities can help environmentally friendly businesses enhance their public image and self-esteem, improve customer loyalty, attract more consumers, and contribute to boosting environmental strategies and interventions in developing countries.
